Inflation is really important, because it discourages hoarding money (since your money is losing real-world value just sitting there) and so it encourages investment.

If you think of the economy as being like a 'sea' where the water is money, then inflation rate is the temperature. When the inflation rate hits zero, the water freezes. Money is getting more valuable, not less, as time goes by, so investors hoard money instead of spending it, and everything stops. No investment equals no new projects equals no construction, no research and development, no industry. And without those things, you get no jobs. And without jobs, you get no consumer spending.
